## Pulse

<!-- [TEST-FIXTURE-PLACEHOLDER: pulse not supplied by world § 8.1 S027 specimen] -->
- title: Twenty pounds on the cloth at Holywell
- one sentence: You brought the Queen's twenty pounds from Whitehall to Holywell, saw five pounds of charges taken off, and received thirty-seven shillings and sixpence for your eighth part.
- details: You went by water from Old Swan Stairs to the outer precinct at Whitehall with Kemp and Richard Burbage to collect the twenty pounds on the warrant dated 15 March 1594, then walked back by the Strand and Holborn. At James Burbage's house in Holywell, Heminges counted sixteen angels, four sovereigns, and eight pounds in silver on the cloth. After sixteen shillings for boat-hire, thirty-four shillings in rewards, and fifty shillings to the Cheapside mercer, fifteen pounds remained to divide into eight parts, one for the stock and thirty-seven shillings and sixpence to each sharer.

## Briefing for tomorrow morning

<!-- [TEST-FIXTURE-PLACEHOLDER: briefing not supplied by world § 8.1 S027 specimen] -->
- coverage: Saturday holds the reckoning at Holywell for the Queen's twenty pounds, the table photo, and your ledger entry at St Helen's.
- Heminges counted twenty pounds on the cloth and took five pounds off for Greenwich boat-hire, rewards, and the Cheapside mercer.
- Seven sharers took thirty-seven shillings and sixpence each, and the stock kept the eighth share.
- Eight shillings for Edith Kettlewood comes out of the stock on Thursday.
- You mean to put your share on a hired horse for Warwickshire in Lent.

### Transcript

[00:00] john_heminges: Set it down there. No, on the cloth, Will, on the cloth, I'll not chase an angel under the settle. A warrant has no weight until someone brings the coin. You've brought it. So. Twenty pound. Count it with me, somebody honest.
[00:08] will_kemp: Count it with me. I'm first on the Queen's paper. William Kemp, William Shakespeare and Richard Burbage. I heard the clerk read it. He read me loudest.
[00:15] richard_burbage: He read you first because he began at the wrong end and was too proud to turn about. And we stood an hour in his passage while he trimmed his quills.
[00:22] william_shakespeare: He read us as servants to the Lord Chamberlain, all three, and looked at us as a man looks at three fish. I never felt so paid and so little.
[00:29] james_burbage: What's the date on it?
[00:35] william_shakespeare: Whitehall, the fifteenth of March, fifteen ninety-four.
[00:41] will_kemp: Ninety-four! There. We played at Christmas, they pay us in Lent, and they date it a year gone. That's the Queen's arithmetic. But I'm first on it.
[00:48] john_heminges: It's ninety-four till Lady Day, as you well know, and it's twenty pound in any year. Sixteen angels at ten shillings, that's eight pound. Four sovereigns, twelve. And eight pound in white money, shillings and sixpences. Twenty, sound and unclipped.
[00:57] thomas_pope: That makes twenty, even when spoken slowly.
[01:03] richard_burbage: And Alleyn's crew had thirty for three nights at Greenwich. Next Christmas we play three, or I eat my buskins.
[01:10] william_shakespeare: Let them have their thirty, Dick. They'll spend it on elm boards. Henslowe has carpenters coming in on Monday.
[01:17] john_heminges: Thirteen, six and eight for the two plays. Six, thirteen and four of Her Majesty's reward. Now. Item.
[01:24] thomas_pope: Here it comes. Hide your purses, lads, John has said Item.
[01:30] john_heminges: Item, boat-hire to Greenwich and home, two days, and the carriage of the baskets. Sixteen shillings.
[01:37] richard_burbage: Sixteen! Did we go by way of Calais?
[01:43] john_heminges: We went against the tide, at Christmas, with a dog. Item, rewards. Five hired men at four shillings. Three boys at two. The book-keeper and the tireman, four apiece. Thirty-four shillings.
[01:51] augustine_phillips: Give the boys three, John. Nick stood two hours in that farthingale and never once scratched.
[01:58] john_heminges: Two is written. I'll give them the third in pies, and it'll please them better. Item. The— the mercer in Cheapside. For the taffeta, and the copper lace, and the Princess's gown that is still not paid for. Fifty shillings.
[02:06] will_kemp: Fifty shillings on a gown for a play the Queen's never seen!
[02:12] william_shakespeare: The town has seen it three times, Will. You were in it. You spoke five-and-thirty lines more than I wrote, and a whole song, and I've put nine of them in the book.
[02:20] will_kemp: Only nine?
[02:26] william_shakespeare: The rest were about the gown.
[02:32] john_heminges: Sixteen, thirty-four and fifty. That is five pound, to the penny. Which leaves fifteen. Fifteen pound in eight parts is thirty-seven shillings and sixpence the part.
[02:40] will_kemp: Eight parts. I count seven men at this board. Who's the eighth, the dog?
[02:46] john_heminges: The stock. As always. The apparel, the books, the licence money. The stock takes a share and I keep it, and when your motley splits, Will Kemp, the stock will buy you another.
[02:54] will_kemp: Then let the stock pay Mistress Kettlewood first. She's owed for a prince's sleeves since the autumn, and she looks at me in the tiring-house as if I wore them.
[03:02] john_heminges: Thursday. Out of the stock. Eight shillings.
[03:08] william_shakespeare: Eight shillings. She required me to remember it.
[03:14] augustine_phillips: Sensible woman.
[03:20] will_kemp: Then I say this. The Queen's reward, the six, thirteen and four, that's a reward for pleasing. Who pleased? When her ladies were nodding on Innocents' night and the candles guttered, who gave them the jig and woke the whole Presence? I say the reward goes by desert.
[03:29] richard_burbage: By desert! God's my life. Then give it all to the dog.
[03:35] james_burbage: By desert I'd have the rent of my house out of it before any of you saw a groat. Who keeps a roof over this company? And two years left on the ground, and Giles Allen sniffing at my timber…
[03:43] richard_burbage: Father. Not the lease. Not before dinner.
[03:49] william_shakespeare: Will, hear me. If we pay by desert we must first agree what each man deserves, and we shall be here till Easter and come out with nothing but opinions. Pay it by the share and we'll all go to dinner equally wronged.
[03:57] thomas_pope: Equally wronged! Write that over the door.
[04:03] will_kemp: You've a smooth tongue, Master Shakespeare. I've noted it. It goes round a man like a cat.
[04:10] william_shakespeare: It's my whole living. I have no dog.
[04:16] augustine_phillips: Take your thirty-seven and six, Will, and I'll set you a new jig for Easter, and you shall have the whole stage after the play and nobody's lines to trouble you.
[04:24] will_kemp: …With the slippers?
[04:30] augustine_phillips: With the slippers.
[04:36] will_kemp: Hm. Well. Count it out, then. But I was first on the paper.
[04:42] john_heminges: You were first on the paper. I'll write that in the book, if it will content you. Kemp. First on the paper. Thirty-seven and six. Richard. Thirty-seven and six. Will.
[04:50] william_shakespeare: Thank you, John. …It's lighter than I thought the Queen would be.
[04:56] will_kemp: John, you will never be troubled by a false report from your own mouth.
[05:02] john_heminges: I am troubled sufficiently by the rest of yours.
[05:08] richard_burbage: Come to the Bull and drink the Queen's health, all of you. Lent or no Lent.
[05:14] william_shakespeare: One cup. Mistress Ansell can smell a tavern through two oak doors, and she has opinions on sack in Lent.
[05:21] richard_burbage: And what will you do with the rest of yours?
[05:27] william_shakespeare: Put it on a horse.
[05:33] thomas_pope: A wager? You?
[05:39] william_shakespeare: A hired one. As far as Warwickshire. I'm going home for Lent, and I mean to arrive like a man who has been paid.
[05:46] james_burbage: And come back, mind. Easter Monday. There's a house to open.
[05:52] william_shakespeare: I'll come back. I've a king wants writing, and nowhere in Stratford to put him.

### Sense

<!-- [TEST-FIXTURE-PLACEHOLDER: sense not supplied by world § 8.1 S027 specimen] -->
- summary: Heminges counted the twenty pounds on the cloth in sixteen angels, four sovereigns, and eight pounds of white money. Five pounds in charges left fifteen pounds to divide into eight parts of thirty-seven shillings and sixpence, with the eighth part kept for the stock and eight shillings set for Edith Kettlewood on Thursday. You talked Kemp down from dividing the reward by desert, took your thirty-seven shillings and sixpence, and said you would put it on a hired horse for Warwickshire.

### Activity

<!-- [TEST-FIXTURE-PLACEHOLDER: activity/story not supplied by world § 8.1 S027 specimen] -->
- title: Divided the Queen's twenty pounds into eight parts at Holywell
- story: You brought the bag to James Burbage's table and watched Heminges count twenty pounds in gold and silver. After sixteen shillings for Greenwich boat-hire, thirty-four shillings in rewards, and fifty shillings to the Cheapside mercer, fifteen pounds went into eight shares of thirty-seven shillings and sixpence. You reminded Heminges of Edith Kettlewood's eight shillings, persuaded Kemp to take his equal share rather than argue desert, and said your share would go toward hiring a horse home for Lent while George Bryan looked on in silence.
- participation:
  - william_shakespeare: Gave the warrant date, argued for equal shares, and took thirty-seven shillings and sixpence for a hired horse to Warwickshire.
  - john_heminges: Counted the twenty pounds, deducted five pounds of charges, and paid out thirty-seven shillings and sixpence per share while holding the stock's part.
  - will_kemp: Boasted of standing first on the warrant, argued for payment by desert, and settled when Phillips promised a new Easter jig with the slippers.
  - richard_burbage: Complained of the passage wait and the sixteen-shilling boat-hire, and invited the fellows to the Bull.
  - james_burbage: Asked the warrant's date, raised the Theatre lease, and told you to return by Easter Monday.
  - thomas_pope: Verified the count and praised your phrase "equally wronged."
  - augustine_phillips: Spoke for the boys' rewards and settled Kemp with the promise of an Easter jig.
  - george_bryan: Attended the reckoning in silence.

- relations: william_shakespeare → will_kemp · works-with · persuaded Kemp to divide by the share rather than desert · "Pay it by the share and we'll all go to dinner equally wronged."
